name: ledger
wording: the record of a context's cuts and their work packages, kept as an append-only sequence of events, each one transition of one cut or work package carrying an id of its own, so a transition recorded once is refused when repeated; its events are taken from the harness's own account of its agents as it happens, never from an agent remembering to record them: a work package is dispatched when its builder is dispatched, returned when its builder returns, and approved when both of its cut's assayers' verdicts return passing it; a verdict with a finding against it returns it to build, and while the assayers disagree it stays unapproved until the architect settles the meaning question; a cut is in flight from its first dispatch and complete once every one of its work packages is approved; each cut's phase, its work packages' status and the work packages ready to dispatch next are computed from it on request; it is versioned with its cut's feature branch, so it shows the state of the branch being read and lands with the cut's merge.
reason: The illustrator's boundary on the reconstitution cut: approval did not say what failing or disagreeing verdicts do; judgment already sends a finding back to the builders and a disagreement to the architect, and the ledger now records exactly that.
